Subject: Embeddings migration: vector dims, batching, normalization & SDK next steps

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great overview of NimbleSearch's current vector search stack and the migration goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared plan: 

Summary from our call:
- Current provider: Pinecone; you export existing vectors and want to migrate to Redwood Dedicated to reduce latency and lower per-query cost.
- Typical vectors: 1536 dim (text-embedding-ada-002) for production; some older indices have 768-dim legacy rows.
- Peak ingestion: ~6k vectors/hour, bulk backfills up to ~120k vectors/day.
- Query QPS: 150qps at 95th percentile; tail latency is the main driver for migrating to dedicated pools.

Immediate action items / asks (what I'll help with):
1) You to share the current export (sample attached) so our infra team can profile dims / normalization.
2) We'll validate dimensional compatibility and recommend whether to (a) keep 1536 and reindex everything, or (b) support mixed dims with per-index variant.
3) Dev to share recommended batching profile and SDK sample for auth + routing to dedicated pool (we've attached a sample config).
4) Decide on whether to store L2-normalized vectors (cosine via normalized vectors) vs storing raw vectors and applying normalization at query time.

Proposed timeline:
- Today: you send sample export (you attached in reply ok)
- 24-48h: Redwood SEs run a quick profile and share recommended batch sizing + normalization approach
- 1 week: POC reindex of a single collection and run latency/cost comparison

Technical notes I promised to surface:
- We support both storing raw vectors and storing pre-normalized vectors. If you rely on cosine similarity in Pinecone today, storing L2-normalized vectors simplifies scoring and is slightly cheaper at query time.
- Batching: we suggest starting with 256 per-request for CPU-backed backfills and 1024-2048 when using GPU-backed ingestion for higher throughput. Exact number depends on average text length and embedding model.
- SDK & auth: Redwood SDKs support API key auth and header-based routing to dedicate pools (x-redwood-pool). I'll loop in Dev for the config snippet.

I've attached the sample export you mentioned and a starter redwood-sample-config.yaml.

Next: Alex, can you confirm the attached export is representative (full vs sampled) and whether you want to normalize on write? Also confirm ideal POC window next week.

Thanks,

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Embeddings migration: vector dims, batching, normalization & SDK next steps

Hi Alex / Priya — Dev on SE. Thanks for the sample — I profiled the CSV quickly and flagged the mixed dims. A few specific recommendations and a config snippet below.

Short answers to your questions:
1) Legacy 768-dim vectors: we recommend keeping them in a separate index/collection during an initial POC. That avoids mixing dims in the same index which complicates similarity calculations. For long-term, best practice is re-embedding to 1536 (via the same embedding model) during a reindex job if content is available. If not, you can create a fallback that queries both indices and merges results by score.
2) Normalization: Redwood supports both approaches. Pre-normalizing (L2) and storing the normalized vectors is slightly cheaper at query time because similarity becomes an inner product; runtime normalization adds CPU per-query. For your 150 qps tail, pre-normalize if you can. If you need mixed sources, we can normalize on read for those rows.
3) Batching / throughput: for bulk backfills we’ve seen stable throughput with batch_size 512 on cloud GPU workers (NVIDIA A10/A100) and 128–256 on CPU workers. For your 120k/day backfill we’d recommend a GPU-backed pipeline for the shortest window. Cost difference rough order: GPU-backed pipeline is ~3–5x throughput per worker compared to CPU but costs more per-hour; we can model this in the POC.

SDK/auth/routing sample (paste into redwood-sample-config.yaml):

# redwood-sample-config.yaml
api_key: "REDACTED_API_KEY"
model: "open-embed-1536"
pool_routing:
  mode: "header"  # options: header | token | automatic
  header_name: "x-redwood-pool"
batching:
  embeddings:
    batch_size: 512
    max_tokens_per_batch: 262144
normalization:
  store_pre_normalized: true
  norm_type: "l2"

HTTP example (python requests):
headers = {
  "Authorization": "Bearer REDACTED_API_KEY",
  "x-redwood-pool": "nimblesearch-prod-pool"
}
response = requests.post("https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings", json={"inputs": [... ]}, headers=headers)

Migration helper notes:
- Incremental reindexing: create a parallel index, write new 1536 vectors, run shadow queries to verify parity, then swap aliases for zero-downtime cutover.
- If you pre-normalize, include a flag in metadata: vector_norm: 1.0 so we can detect mixed sources.
- We can provide a small reindexing script (python) as part of the POC.

I’ve attached the sample config (redwood-sample-config.yaml) with the snippet above and a small reindex helper we can share privately. If you want, we can also run a short benchmark next week against a 10k subset to compare latency and cost.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
